rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a rental property owner, coordinator, or multiple persons to use algorithmic software, coordinate sensitive information, or engage in parallel pricing coordination to set or recommend rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels for residential dwellings.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental dwelling units statewide, excluding inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to conducting research or statistical analysis without setting prices, public rental databases, real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms, or government entities setting rents through affordability controls.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for: a. a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator; b. a coordinator to facilitate a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition with respect to residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating function; c. two or more persons to engage in or otherwise facilitate parallel pricing coordination; d. any agent or representative of a coordinator or subcontractor thereof to engage in parallel pricing coordination; or e. any person to perform a coordinating function.
